explain: Recheck the source revision immediately before activation so expensive preparation does not publish a snapshot that has already been superseded.
steps: Prepare artifacts for revision 2. || Compare against the current authoritative revision before moving the active pointer.

explain: Stage artifacts are reusable only when their recorded inputs and processing profiles match. A crash does not make partial preparation active search state.
steps: Record which stages have completed. || Resume at the first absent artifact without treating the incomplete generation as published.
name: stage-artifacts

explain: A failed replacement is quarantined according to an explicit lifecycle policy. Nonempty input producing zero chunks must not silently replace a usable old revision.
steps: Detect an invalid prepared replacement. || Keep the old active revision and record a safe failure category.
name: poison-document

explain: A collection-scoped lock coordinates only participants using the same lock convention. It does not freeze source files or stop external services from changing state.
steps: Represent the lock and the independently mutable source. || Change the source revision while the collection lock is held.
name: advisory-lock-scope

explain: Timing claims require measured observations and workload context. The toy percentile calculation shows why a single fast sample does not establish a tail-latency guarantee.
steps: Sort observed durations for the fixture. || Select a declared nearest-rank percentile instead of summing stage percentiles.
name: measured-latency
